title: [D1 Ingest] Quarantine invalid input without stalling the stream
summary: Quarantine now lives in the engine. `sql/migrations/0003_ingest_quarantine.sql` creates `helena_ingest_quarantine` — ingestion identity, raw-record reference, the contract version that refused it, the typed ParseFailure and the payload as BYTEA exactly as read, keyed on (tenant, sensor, capture_sha256, record_offset) — plus the plain view `helena_ingest_quarantine_counts` grouped by reason. `helena.normalizer.Quarantine` writes and reads them and `Normalizer.ingest_capture(capture, quarantine)` is the ingestion path: it yields the events, routes every refusal to the table with its raw line, and carries on. `QuarantineCounts` joins the engine-side numerator to the capture's own record count and refuses a total that does not reconcile. 13 new tests, the engine-side ones executed against a real RisingWave; the suite is 409 passed.
assumption_validated: That the single-store invariant survives contact with quarantine — that a refused record can be kept as a typed row in the streaming engine, with its bytes intact, without a second store and without stalling the stream. It does. Demonstrated by execution rather than asserted: a malformed record in the middle of a capture is stored while the records on either side normalize with their real offsets; BYTEA round-trips a line that is not valid UTF-8 unchanged (measured on RisingWave 3.0.3), which is what makes 'exactly as read' true rather than 'as read, if it decoded'; and over a 63-record capture built from the 62 real records of data/ingest/flow-sample.jsonl with one field-drifted record and one non-UTF-8 line, 61 events came out, 2 rows went in, and the counter reconciled (rate 0.0317, contract_violation 1, malformed_json 1, not_this_format 0). What is NOT validated: the 'without stalling' claim is demonstrated over a capture on disk, not a live consumer — there is no broker on this path yet.
makes_buildable: Task 10 (broker wiring) has the destination for the refusals it will consume and the one call that routes them — `Normalizer.ingest_capture` — so the consumer does not need its own quarantining path, and it has two of its three ingest counters already reconciling (`QuarantineCounts.records/quarantined/by_reason`); the third, `normalized`, is a subtraction here and becomes an engine-side count in the increment that stores an event, reconciling against this subtraction rather than replacing it. Task 11 (replay driver) has the idempotence it needs: re-ingesting a capture rewrites the same quarantine rows rather than doubling them, so a replayed capture does not inflate the rate — tested. Task 12 (flatten layer) has the pattern for a migration that creates a table and a plain view over it and asserts the Python name constants against information_schema by asking the engine. Anything watching for input drift has the number ADR-0010 said to watch, with a runbook section (docs/runbook.md §6) saying what each reason means and that the answer to a high rate is a new observation of the input, not a loosened field.

verification.detail: 409 passed in 17.9 s, run twice: once against an engine already up, once cold with nothing running (the conftest fixture starts an in-memory RisingWave). 13 new tests, 9 of them marked `integration` and executing the new SQL against a real engine via the `migrated_engine` fixture — no test asserts on SQL text. Migration 0003 was also applied by hand with `uv run scripts/migrate.py` against a live engine (three files applied, status clean), and both SQL snippets printed in docs/runbook.md §6 were executed against it over a capture built from the 62 real records of data/ingest/flow-sample.jsonl with two records corrupted: 61 events, 2 quarantine rows, counter reconciled. Mutation-checked: narrowing the primary key to (capture_sha256, record_offset) makes test_two_tenants_quarantining_one_capture_do_not_overwrite_each_other fail with one tenant's row silently gone — the cross-tenant claim is a real assertion, not a comparison of a value with itself. Column types probed against RisingWave 3.0.3 before being written: BYTEA round-trips invalid UTF-8, a composite PRIMARY KEY is accepted, and a plain VIEW with GROUP BY over a table selects correctly.

deferred: The 'ingest counters' half of PRD step 3. The step says 'expose a quarantine rate counter ALONGSIDE the ingest counters' and there are no ingest counters — task 10's own steps are where 'records consumed, normalized, quarantined' is listed, and nothing consumes from a broker or stores a normalized event yet. What exists is the quarantine counter with the only denominator that exists (`Capture.record_count`, because the broker is consume-once), so the rate is computable and reconciles today; `QuarantineCounts.normalized` is a documented subtraction, exact because `normalize_capture` yields exactly one result per record, and it is the value task 10's engine-side count should reconcile against.

A timestamp column on a quarantine row. Deliberate and argued in ADR-0013: a wall clock makes a replayed capture produce a different row from the run it replays (ADR-0011's reason for keeping one off the event), and under the upsert the stored value would silently mean 'the last time this was refused'. When a record arrived is a property of an ingest run, and nothing records runs yet — the increment that does owns adding it.

A version set on the quarantine row. `VersionSet` requires all eight dimensions and seven do not exist yet (ADR-0008); stamping one here means inventing seven constants for a row no assessment cites. The two things that actually determined the row are recorded: `schema_version` (EVENT_SCHEMA_VERSION, the contract that refused it) and `input_format`. ADR-0012 deferred 'an adapter version on ParseFailure' to this increment — adapters still have no version of their own, and this table is where one belongs when they do.

Routing `CaptureError` to quarantine. An offset that addresses no record still raises, unchanged from task 8: the bytes were never read, so it is this deployment's bug rather than input drift, and quarantining it would file a producer's name against our own mistake. So 'route EVERY typed parse or validation failure' is scoped to the ones that are facts about the input — the three ParseFailure reasons.

Logging. Nothing on this path emits a log line, for the same reason tasks 7 and 8 gave: `helena.observability.logger` needs Settings and there is no ingest run to attribute a line to. The counter is a store query, which is the more durable surface anyway.

A second copy of EVENT_SCHEMA_VERSION in SQL. Task 7's handover said the increment that first creates a table holding a normalized event must add the SQL copy and the equality test. This table holds records that did NOT become events, and the version is written as data by the one Python constant rather than declared as a literal in the migration — so there is still no second copy to drift, and the obligation still belongs to the increment that stores an event.

Truncation of a large payload. Nothing truncates, so there is no visible-truncation marker to design. If a producer ever sends a line large enough to matter, adding a limit means adding the marker with it — `concept/instruction.md` §2, truncation is visible or it is a bug.
lessons: task 09: RisingWave 3.0.3 measured for the quarantine columns before they were written: BYTEA round-trips bytes that are not valid UTF-8 unchanged (b'{"id":"\xff"}' came back byte-identical), a composite PRIMARY KEY (four columns) is accepted, and a plain VIEW with a GROUP BY over a table creates and selects fine. psycopg returns a BYTEA column as `bytes`; `count(*)` in a view comes back as a Python int (so a strict NonNegativeInt field accepts it), while `sum(count(*))` in a query over that view comes back as `Decimal` — a strict int field would reject that, so aggregate in Python or cast.

task 09: The quarantine primary key has to carry tenant and sensor, not just the raw-record reference, and the reason is task 04's measurement: an INSERT onto an existing key in RisingWave is a silent upsert. Mutation-checked this session — narrowing the key to (capture_sha256, record_offset) makes one tenant's row vanish under the other's with no error. The same upsert is what makes replay idempotent, so it is a feature once the key is right.

task 09: `tests/test_normalizer.py` already had a module-level helper called `_mangled`; a second one with the same name appended to the file shadowed the first and broke an unrelated task-08 test with a TypeError about a missing positional argument. The file is 1500 lines with helpers scattered through it — grep for a helper name before defining one, because the failure surfaces in a distant test.

task 09: The `not_this_format` reason can only be produced by an adapter for a format that declares itself, so a test that wants all three reasons in one capture has to read it with `flow-envelope`, not `flow-json`. A flat-format line reaching the flat adapter can only be `contract_violation` or `malformed_json` (task 08 pinned that asymmetry).

task 09: Quarantine writes deliberately do not FLUSH — a RisingWave row is unreadable until a flush, so flushing per refused record would put a synchronous round trip in the middle of the stream, which is the stall the increment exists to avoid. `Quarantine.stored` and `Quarantine.counts` flush before reading instead. The consequence, stated in ADR-0013: a count taken through another connection while ingestion is still running may lag.

task 09: `QuarantineCounts` evaluates its own reconciliation in a Pydantic `model_validator(mode='after')` — per-reason totals must add up to `quarantined`, `quarantined` must not exceed `records`, and `by_reason` must carry all three reasons including zeros. That turns the definition-of-done's 'counts reconcile' into something the suite runs rather than a claim, and it is cheap: three `if`s on a frozen model. Worth copying for the D2 reconciliation view's Python side.

task 09: `concept/08-open-questions.md`'s 'where quarantined records live' is now closed by docs/decisions/0013-quarantine-in-the-single-store.md. The other two cross-cutting-and-urgent items in that section are still open: the record silently lost at a catch-up boundary (which is why replayability is a goal rather than a claim), and durability/backup for the single store.
failed_approaches: task 09: Storing the payload in a VARCHAR column was rejected before it was written. Task 08 measured that invalid UTF-8 in a line raises UnicodeDecodeError from json.loads and is reported as malformed_json — so exactly the records most worth quarantining are the ones a text column would have to refuse or decode lossily, and a quarantine row that lost the bytes that caused it cannot be diagnosed. BYTEA was probed against the engine first.

task 09: Putting a `quarantined_at TIMESTAMPTZ` on the row was considered and rejected. It would break the property task 11 is about to test (a capture replayed twice produces identical rows) for this table, and under the composite-key upsert the stored value would silently mean 'the last time this was refused' rather than 'when it was first seen' — a field that looks like provenance and is not. Arrival time is a property of an ingest run.

task 09: Writing the event id onto a quarantine row was considered and rejected. The digest computes perfectly well from tenant, sensor, capture and offset even for a refused record, which is exactly why it is tempting — and it would assert an event identity for something that never became an event, contradicting `Normalizer.normalize`'s rule that no identity is stamped on a record that never became an observation. The primary key addresses the row instead, and a test pins the field set of `QuarantinedRecord`.

task 09: Giving `ingest_capture` its own loop over `read_capture` was rejected: it would have made two places that read a capture and stamp identity, which is the parallel path `concept/03-architecture.md` forbids. Both `normalize_capture` and `ingest_capture` now go through one private `_results(capture)` generator yielding (offset, raw line, result) — the raw line has to be carried alongside because a `ParseFailure` deliberately holds no copy of the input it refused and an event holds only the parsed observation.

task 09: Letting `Quarantine.counts` compute the rate over zero records as 0.0 was rejected — it reads as 'nothing was refused' when the truth is 'nothing was read'. It raises instead, and a test pins it. `describe_capture` really can return record_count 0 (an empty file), so this is reachable.
next_session_should_know: Ingest a capture through `Normalizer.ingest_capture(capture, quarantine)` — it yields only `NormalizedEvent`s, writes every refusal to the engine with its raw line, and does not stop. `normalize_capture` still exists and still yields `NormalizedEvent | ParseFailure` for callers that want to see both; if you use it, you own the failures, and nothing stores them for you. Build the quarantine with `Quarantine(connection=<psycopg autocommit connection>, identity=settings.identity)`. Six things that will bite otherwise. (1) `ingest_capture` REFUSES a quarantine whose identity is not the normalizer's, with a `ConfigurationError` — the two are configured from the same `Settings` and that is the only combination that works, deliberately. (2) The quarantine primary key is (tenant, sensor, capture_sha256, record_offset); re-ingesting rewrites the same rows rather than doubling, so replay does not inflate the rate — do not add a timestamp or an event id to the row without reading ADR-0013 first, both were rejected on purpose. (3) `QuarantineCounts` refuses to exist if its numbers do not reconcile, and `by_reason` always carries all three reasons including zeros; `normalized` is `records - quarantined`, a subtraction that is exact only because `normalize_capture` yields one result per record — task 10's engine-side normalized count should reconcile AGAINST it, not replace it. (4) A rate over a capture with no records raises rather than returning 0.0. (5) Writes do not FLUSH; the two read methods do, so a count taken from a different connection mid-run may lag. (6) `CaptureError` (an offset addressing no record) still raises and is NOT quarantined — that is this deployment's bug, not the producer's. docs/runbook.md §6 is the operator's page for all of it, including what a rising `contract_violation` rate means and that the answer is a new observation of the input rather than a loosened field. Note the runbook's old '§6 When something is wrong' is now §7; nothing referenced it by number. Still true and unchanged: no event is stored in the engine, nothing consumes from the broker, `EVENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` still has one home (this table writes it as data, not as a SQL literal, so there is still no second copy to assert equal), capture identity is provisional under live ingestion (ADR-0010), `bin/README.md` still points at a `scripts/build-binaries.sh` that does not exist, and there is still no git repository, so nothing here was committed. One small stale statement noticed and left alone: `docs/decisions/0007-sql-migrations.md` says `sql/migrations/` holds the ledger and nothing else — true when it was written at D0, false since migration 0002, and it is a dated record rather than a live claim.
